sentences.text: As per the case of the petitioners, on 06.05.2018 at about 3.00 p.m. the petitioner in MVC No.5799/2018 being the driver of Bus bearing No. KA 483536 and the petitioners in other petitions being the passengers, were proceeding in the ssaid Bus following traffic rules and in a careful manner from Dharmasthala towards Bengaluru.

When the said Bus reached near Palguni Village, Banakal Hobli, Mudigere Taluk, Chikkamagaluru District on NH234 Road, the KSRTC Bus bearing No. KA19F3075 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner came from opposite direction and dashed against the said Bus.

Due to the said impact, the petitioner in MVC No.
5799/2018 being the driver and the petitioners in other petitions being the passengers of the said privateBus sustained grievous injuries.

23. As discussed herein above, the respondent has examined its driver as R.W.1.

But except the oral statement of R.W.1, there is absolutely no material forthcoming from the respondent to prove that there was any negligence or at least contributory negligence on the part of the driver of the private Bus, who is the petitioner in MVC No.5799/2018 in the said accident.
24. As submitted by the learned Counsel for the petitioners, sketch in the spot mahazar at Ex.P.4 would show that accident occurred on the left side of the road from Banakal towards Mudigere.
It is undisputed fact that the private Bus was proceeding from Dharmasthala towards Bengaluru and the KSRTC Bus was coming from opposite direction.

Hence, from the place of 21 MVC No.5799/18 c/w.5801,5803,5804,5806/2018/2018 accident shown in the spot mahazar Ex. P.4, it would clearly show that the KSRTC Bus came towards right side of the road and dashed to the private Bus.
Therefore, the accident took place on the wrong side of the KSRTC Bus.
It is true that in cross examination of P.W.2 it is elicited that the private Bus was proceeding from up gradient towards lower gradient and the KSRTC Bus was proceeding from up gradient route.
But mere fact that private Bus was proceeding in down gradient does not make out a case to show that the private Bus was driven in a rash and negligent manner.
On the other hand, as discussed herein above, the accident took place on the wrong side of the KSRTC Bus.

27. Issue No.3 in MVC No.5799/2018:
From the discussion made herein above, it is clear that the petitioner suffered open grade III B comminuted fracture both bones of right leg with open wound over inferolateral aspect of left knee.
He was treated as inpatient at V.P. Magnus Hospital for the period of 9 days and he underwent surgery.
The said facts is proved by the document at Ex.P.30.
Therefore, considering the nature of the injuries suffered and the period of treatment taken by the petitioner, he is entitled to compensation under the head Pain and Agony.

In the circumstances of the case, an amount of Rs.40,000/ would be proper and reasonable compensation payable to the petitioner under the head Pain and Agony and therefore, a compensation of Rs.40,000/ is awarded in favour of the petitioner under the head pain and agony.
As per the contention of the petitioner, he spent Rs.2,00,000/ towards his medical expenses and other expenses.
The petitioner has deposed in his chief examination that he spent more than Rs.2,00,000/ towards medical expenses, nourishment and other incidental charges.
But there is no independent evidence to prove the said contention.
On the other hand, the petitioner has produced 3 medical bills as per Ex.P.29.

As per the said bills, the petitioner spent Rs.69,775/,
which includes the ambulance bill for the amount of Rs.6,000/.
Therefore, the documents produced by the petitioner do not prove that he spent Rs.2,00,000/ for his medical treatment.
29. However, the fact that the petitioner sustained fracture injury and he was treated as inpatient for 9 days at V.P. Magnus Hospital stands not controverted.

Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for Roshan Ahmad vs K.S.R.T.C on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101866879/
10 Rs.69,775/ regarding the bills at Ex.P.29 towards expenses incurred by him for his treatment.
